definitions.explanation: A person who buys popular or limited items and resells them at a higher price for profit. The term carries a negative connotation, implying unfair or exploitative behavior.

examples.japanese: {転売|てんばい}ヤーのせいでチケットが{買|か}えない。
examples.english: I can't buy tickets because of scalpers.

examples.japanese: {限定品|げんていひん}が{転売|てんばい}ヤーに{買|か}い{占|し}められた。
examples.english: The limited-edition items were bought up by resellers.

examples.japanese: {転売|てんばい}ヤー{対策|たいさく}として、{一人|ひとり}{一点|いってん}{限|かぎ}りの{購入|こうにゅう}{制限|せいげん}が{設|もう}けられた。
examples.english: As a measure against scalpers, a limit of one item per person was put in place.

notes:
USAGE:
A colloquial term combining {転売|てんばい} (resale) with the suffix ヤー (from English '-er'). Strongly negative, used to criticize people who buy up popular goods to resell at inflated prices. Common targets include concert tickets, limited-edition goods, and popular electronics.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {転売|てんばい}ヤー{対策|たいさく} (anti-scalper measures)
- {転売|てんばい}ヤーに{買|か}い{占|し}められる (to be bought up by scalpers)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {転売|てんばい}{屋|や}: same meaning, slightly more traditional phrasing
